{'translation': 'Apple is celebrating its 50th anniversary this year, and plenty of its customers are older than that. Apple has recently added a new support page that rounds up 50 ways to make its devices easier to use — most of them by way of accessibility settings.', 'explanation': '', 'reasoning': ''}

{'translation': 'From adjusting the font size on your Apple Watch to having your iPhone notify you when the washing machine has finished its cycle, the tips run the gamut...', 'explanation': '', 'reasoning': ''}

{'translation': 'Apple says its goal is to make its technology available to everyone — including older adults.', 'explanation': '', 'reasoning': ''}

{'translation': "At Apple, we believe the best technology should work for everyone — including older adults. So our products and services are designed with that in mind, with built-in accessibility features that help you connect, create, and do the things you love in whatever way works best for you. The way we engage with the world changes as life does. From making text on screen larger to making conversations clearer in a noisy restaurant, Apple's ecosystem of devices, features, and services is designed to meet your needs.", 'explanation': '', 'reasoning': ''}

{'translation': 'The support page focuses on accessibility features and is divided into 10 main categories.', 'explanation': '', 'reasoning': ''}

  • {'translation': 'Vision: See your screen more comfortably', 'explanation': '', 'reasoning': ''}
  • {'translation': 'Hearing: Stay connected to conversations, alerts, and your surroundings', 'explanation': '', 'reasoning': ''}
  • {'translation': 'Mobility: Adjust how you operate and control your devices', 'explanation': '', 'reasoning': ''}
  • {'translation': 'Speech: Speak in your own way', 'explanation': '', 'reasoning': ''}
  • {'translation': 'Cognitive: Focus on the present and stay in control', 'explanation': '', 'reasoning': ''}
  • {'translation': 'Personalization: Make it yours', 'explanation': '', 'reasoning': ''}
  • {'translation': 'Organization: Remember what matters', 'explanation': '', 'reasoning': ''}
  • {'translation': 'Health: Learn about your body with useful insights', 'explanation': '', 'reasoning': ''}
  • {'translation': 'Safety: Help you feel safe and sound', 'explanation': '', 'reasoning': ''}
  • {'translation': 'Connection: Stay in touch', 'explanation': '', 'reasoning': ''}

{'translation': 'Take the Vision category, for example. It includes options for enlarging text, bolding text, inverting colors, setting color filters, reducing transparency, increasing contrast, and reducing motion, among other things. Some features, like Sound Recognition, were pushed hard when Apple first introduced them but have remained largely under the radar.', 'explanation': '', 'reasoning': ''}

{'translation': "Sound Recognition listens for specific sounds and uses on-device intelligence to notify you when it detects them. The feature can recognize 15 different sounds, or you can train your device to listen for your name, as well as unique electronic noises in your environment — like the beeps of kitchen appliances, certain types of alarm systems, or door chimes. On the HomePod, Sound Recognition can also listen for smoke or carbon monoxide alarm sounds. It also works with CarPlay, where your iPhone will listen for and detect sirens, car horns, and even a baby crying. When a designated sound is detected, you'll receive a notification — or, if you're using CarPlay, it'll appear on your car's display.", 'explanation': '', 'reasoning': ''}

{'translation': "The page is an impressively thorough showcase of just how many accessibility features Apple's devices currently offer. Each section offers individual instructions for each supported device — which, depending on the feature, can include the iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV, Vision Pro, and CarPlay.", 'explanation': '', 'reasoning': ''}
